messages.subject: Re: [knitr] How to generate markdown output programmatically?
parts:
Do you mean something like this?

# construct markdown blocks and knit them
src = paste(sprintf('
# Line %s of iris```{r}
iris[%s, ]
```
', 1:nrow(iris), 1:nrow(iris)), collapse = '\n\n')
library(knitr)
knit(text = src, output = 'iris.md')
system('pandoc --toc -s -o iris.html iris.md')
browseURL('iris.html')

Basically it is a matter of manipulating character strings. Here is a
more complicated example:

https://github.com/yihui/knitr-examples/blob/master/041-label-i.Rmd
https://github.com/yihui/knitr-examples/blob/master/041-label-i-child.tpl

Regards,
Yihui

On Fri, Sep 14, 2012 at 4:06 PM, Jim Winget <win...@google.com> wrote:
> I've been trying to automate some of my report generation with knitr, but
> have found an apparent issue that I can't seem to work around. I have some
> rather large sections of code with internal loops that generate ~100 plots.
> I use R/knitr -> markdown -> pandoc -> html. This all works as expected, but
> is less internally structured than I'd like. In particular, I'd like to be
> able to generate index entries (anchors) for each plot to allow a main index
> with links to be generated by panddoc.
>
> To generate nice output, I use markdown generation. The problem arises with
> the need to switch from "asis" to "markdown" output dynamically in the
> execution of a code block. I've tried resetting chunk options dynamically,
> and even defining my own output hook routines with internal tests to see if
> the output should be reformatted or just passed through. Despite several
> attempts, I can't seem to get this to work (perhaps due to buffering).
>
> In the simplest form, I'd like a printASIS(...) function that bypasses the
> current output mode and generates the contemporaneous raw output (in
> particular, buffer flushes may be required to keep things in sync) in-line
> with the other processed output (but avoids all formatting/conversions
> addition of ## comments etc.). This would allow toggling in and out of
> markdown mode. My plan would be to then intercept all plot calls toggle back
> to markdown, insert "markdown headers", and toggle back out, based on the
> titles and subtitles. Since these strings are dynamically constructed, there
> really doesn't appear to be a viable alternative to this extended scripting.
>
> Another use case is to have a few special purpose "print" routines for
> dynamic tables, charts, Google vis plots, etc. In these instances my plan
> would be to generate the appropriate in-line HTML/javascript. I don't plan
> to do this for all output, just selected high value bits. Obviously these
> special "print" routines will fall back to plain print/plot when the output
> is already "as is" for the chunk.
>
> Basically, I'd like to recover some of the functionality and aesthetics I
> had via R2HTML output mechanisms but in knitr.
>
> Any help appreciated. Working code especially appreciated :-)
>
> Thanks,
> Jim
>
> PS: While its possible to run yet another pipeline stage in sed/gawk/perl
> between R/knitr and pandoc to do something akin to this, I haven't found a
> clean way to do it without emitting and parsing special markers to control
> the intermediate transformation. This extra step also makes things less
> hermetic and reproducible.

parts:
Oops, re-posted to the group...

On Mon, Sep 17, 2012 at 4:58 PM, Jim Winget <win...@google.com> wrote:
Yihui

First thanks for the timely response. I've tried to find a reasonable way to apply your (for lack of a better description) "two pass macro expansion" solution to my problem, but it doesn't seem to be a good fit. In part, past experience has convinced me that recursive use of the same features tends to make debugging more challenging.

Perhaps you have another solution that will fit my needs. My several thousand lines of code looks a bit more like this:

-----
# Initialize
Read a large blob of dynamically produced data. The actual variables (column names) and types in the data frame may change from run to run.

# Process
For each variable
   # Define the custom title
   set custom_computed_string = variable name & attributes.
   do some processing, filtering, etc.
      # Update title: custom_computed_string based on processing, etc.
   check the results of this variable against various metrics
   if this variables metrics meet one or more of N possible cases (N~100), then
      generate customized output (tables, plots, etc.) based on the specific case:
      ...
      case i:     myPrint(processed_variable, title=paste(custom_computed_string, "case i:", metrics))
      case i+1: myPlot(processed_variable, title=paste(custom_computed_string, "case i+1:", metrics))
      ...
-----

Now to keep things properly documented, there are numerous points where other less important output is generated in the above calculations. Think of it as providing the background context for the main plots and tables.  However, the most important sections are those associated with a set of specific cases. These are the ones I wanted to use headers for so that they were directly accessible. A single run might produce from 10 to 100 special case outputs. They are kept in a single html doc (with images in-lined) to help preserve context/integrity.

So my hope was to take my existing solution and add the minimal changes. In particular, all of my variable printout and plots go through custom routines, thus the only code changes should be to extend these routines to inject markdown output using the dynamically computed title string.

The solution I've been trying to achieve is to leave all of my current main line code alone with it's output nicely formatted. Then make a few small changes to my custom output routines. In particular, if markdown header generation is enabled than stick a shim layer in my output routines to generate the markdown headers in-line with the print/plot generation:

# Save original function
myOrigPrint <- myPrint

# redefine original function to add new output
myPrint <- function(data, title)
{
   # Invoke output routine to generate the in-line markdown header
   OutputMarkdownHeader(header=title, level=2)
   # invoke the original print routine
   myOrigPrint(data,title)
}

#Similarly for myPlot.

# Where my desired implementation to output markdown looks something like this
# Note that the knitr Get/Set routines are made up. I can't seem to find a way 
# to communicate with the outer knitr environment.

OutputMarkdownHeader <- function(header, level)
{
   # Save current output mode (as-is, markdown, etc.)
   ??? orig_mode = knitrGetMode()
   # Enable output in as-is mode if needed
   ??? knitrSetMode("asis")
   hashes = rep("#",level)
   cat(paste(hashes,header,"\n"))
   # Reset output to original mode
   ??? knitrSetMode(orig_mode)
}

-------------------------------------

I hope that gives you a better idea of the programming extension I'm looking for in knitr. As I mentioned before, I had thought I'd be able to use the output hooks to change the code output behavior based on a global state variable. But I haven't found a way to "communicate" state information from my code being evaluated to the knitr output routine doing reformatting. 

I had thought of just injecting special token strings ("<BEGIN-MARKDOWN>", "<END-MARKDOWN>") and then doing a custom pattern match in the output hook, but it just seems so ugly compared to toggling a single bit.

Further suggestions appreciated,
Jim
